block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: The required down payment varies by buyer, lender, property and purchase structure. For first-time buyers, compare deposit requirements, lender criteria, valuation, income assessment, monthly affordability and whether the specific property is financeable. Confirm current lender terms and property eligibility before relying on mortgage funding for the purchase.

items.answer: The required down payment varies by buyer, lender, property and purchase structure. For first-time buyers, check current lender requirements for income, residency, existing commitments and the buyer profile before treating mortgage funding as available.
items.question: How much down payment should I plan for?

items.answer: Mortgage fit depends on both borrower affordability and the financeability of the property. Include the deposit, registration costs, lender fees, valuation costs and a sensible cash reserve in the amount needed before completion.
items.question: How should I assess whether a mortgage fits the purchase?

items.answer: A mortgage may be possible, but eligibility depends on both the buyer and property. Confirm that the specific property, project status and valuation can support the mortgage route being considered by the buyer.
items.question: Can I get a mortgage?

items.answer: Avoiding overpayment starts with comparing the property against credible alternatives. Identify whether a cheaper option gives up location quality, layout, delivery certainty, demand or another feature that matters to the buyer.
items.question: How do I avoid overpaying?

items.answer: A limited budget works best when the trade-offs are chosen deliberately. A lower price is offset by weaker location, layout, quality, service costs or resale depth. Protect the overall buying case rather than stretching to a headline price, discount or low initial payment.
